idea: Basic plumbing maintenance every homeowner should know
title: Clearing Clogged Faucet Aerators
description: When water pressure suddenly drops at just one faucet, the issue is rarely inside your main water line. In most cases, mineral scale and pipe debris have collected inside the faucet aerator—the small screen assembly threaded onto the tip of the spout. To restore full flow, unscrew the aerator housing counterclockwise, disassemble the mesh screens, and flush away trapped particles. For stubborn mineral scale, soak the components in household vinegar. Cleaning your aerators twice a year prevents localized pressure loss and extends component life. What maintenance task do you check first when flow drops?

visual_story: The visual displays a close-up disassembly of a standard faucet aerator from the spout tip. Viewers can see how mineral particles become trapped against the screen stack, blocking water flow. This clearly illustrates that localized low pressure is caused by physical debris restriction at the terminal outlet rather than a main pipe breakdown.

on_image_text.explanation: Mineral scale and pipe sediment collect inside the aerator screen stack, restricting localized outlet flow.
